observation.visible_scene: A calm, slow-moving river or stream winding through a dense green deciduous forest, filmed from a fixed vantage at the water's edge. A single grey rock protrudes from the surface in the left-center foreground, and the right bank is covered with a mat of green algae/duckweed. The water mirrors the surrounding trees and a pale sky, and fixed lens-flare artifacts (a green dot upper-left and an orange blotch mid-left) overlay the frame. The composition, tree line, rock, and flare positions remain identical from the first to the last sampled frame, indicating a static camera.
visible_changes: The water surface shows continuous subtle motion: small ripples and the texture of the tree/sky reflections shimmer and reconfigure from frame to frame, most visibly in the bright central reflection patch and along the narrowed channel in the distance.

Tiny pale floating specks (small debris/leaf fragments) on the left half of the surface drift slowly and change relative position across the sequence, while the protruding rock and the algae mat stay fixed in place.

The distant center of the stream, where it bends and narrows, displays a persistent, slightly faster ripple pattern consistent with gentle current, without any new object entering or leaving the view.
outside_clip_unknowns: The beginning and end of this clip are arbitrary crop boundaries; the longer source video's full duration, any wind or rainfall events, and what happens before t=0 or after t=2.67s are not shown.
The exact nature of the floating specks (leaves, insects, or foam) and the true flow direction/speed of the current cannot be determined from these frames alone.
uncertain_details: Any camera motion is essentially undetectable; the scene reads as a locked-off shot, so the observed changes are attributed to water surface dynamics rather than panning or zooming.
The shimmering of reflections is a deformation of the reflected image on the moving water, not movement of separate objects on the surface.
